title: Introduce Mini Authoring Lab: compact RAG playground + telemetry probes
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add a compact local-first RAG quickstart (Mini Authoring Lab) with devcontainer, example agent/tool stubs, telemetry probe presets and a smoke CI job. Recommended for onboarding engineers and product proto work.
description:
Context and motivation: Small teams frequently ask for a reproducible, tiny RAG playground they can boot locally to iterate on retrieval + tool-calling patterns without the overhead of full demos. This quickstart (Mini Authoring Lab) is a compact authoring sandbox that demonstrates a minimal retrieval loop, an agent-style tool-calling stub, structured output linting, and lightweight telemetry probes wired to Redwood SDK calls. It is intended for onboarding, guided experiments, and authoring prompt/eval sets.

What this PR includes: - A new quickstarts/mini-authoring-lab directory with a short README, preseeded sample index, and a single-file example agent (node.js + typescript) that shows: retrieval -> candidate scoring -> tool call -> structured response. - Devcontainer and Dockerfile for consistent local environments. - A telemetry probes harness (telemetry/probes.yaml + example probe configs) that demonstrates token/cost sampling and a compact latency histogram export. - Structured-output linter config and a small set of stepwise assertions for local smoke runs. - A CI smoke job that runs the quickstart in headless mode using a small seeded index and validates the final JSON contract.

Checklist (author): [x] Add quickstart files and README; [x] Add devcontainer and runbook; [x] Add minimal telemetry probes and docs; [x] Add smoke CI workflow; [x] Add examples referencing Redwood SDK (TS).

Usage notes: The quickstart is intentionally constrained (small index, short sequence lengths) to make it feasible on a developer laptop. The README contains a 'development vs production' section describing where to swap in Redwood hosted API keys or Dedicated endpoints, how to pin model versions, and recommendations for batching/kv-cache profiles when scaling beyond the mini lab.

Related work and links: Linear ENG-2013 for authoring ergonomics, PM-98 for quickstart prioritization, and SUP-4421 for a customer ask that motivated the telemetry examples.

Testing and validation: Added a lightweight smoke test that uses the included seeded index and runs the agent in headless Node to assert structured JSON output. CI reproduces the smoke run on GitHub Actions.

Migration notes: This is additive; no breaking changes. The quickstart references consolidated SDK helper util functions placed under quickstarts/shared-utils for reuse by other quickstarts.

Contact: Maya Patel (author) for any follow-ups or iteration requests.

review_comments: Ethan Li (reviewer): Nice compact layout. Two asks: add a short note on credentials handling in README (avoid committing keys) and can we make the telemetry sample_rate default to 0.01?
Maya Patel (author): Good catches — added a creds section to README and exposed TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE as an env var with default 0.02 to balance noise and observability for local runs.
Santiago Cortez (reviewer): Can the smoke CI run in <3 mins? Current Docker build took ~7m on my run. Consider using node:alpine and caching the workspace to speed it up.
Maya Patel (author): Switched base image to node:18-bullseye-slim and added a small cache step in the workflow; verified CI runtime dropped to ~2:45 in my fork run.
Priya Nair (approver): LGTM after the CI time reduction and README credential guidance. Small nit in README grammar but not blocking. Approved.

notes_for_maintainers: This quickstart references quickstarts/shared-utils/redwood-sdk-wrap.ts. If that helper moves, update the example imports. Telemetry configs are intentionally conservative for local dev; teams can swap in full sample configs from telemetry/probes/ for staging. The smoke CI job uses small VM specs and should not affect heavier pipelines.
